features: ⚠️ THIS VERSION ADDS A MIGRATION: a new table for ATECO codes. It applies itself with the update and touches no existing data.

THE ATECO CODE NO LONGER HAS TO BE TYPED FROM MEMORY — Next to the «ATECO code» field of the supplier record there is a search button on the official ISTAT classification: 3,257 codes with their titles. You can search by code, or by activity in words, and pick from the list. The field stays editable by hand.

YOU CAN SEE WHERE EACH CODE COMES FROM — Under each result the branch of the classification it belongs to is shown, and next to the code whether it is a category or a subcategory: the chamber of commerce record carries the six-digit code, that is the subcategory, and now it can be told at a glance.

⚠️ ATECO 2025 CHANGED THE NAMES, AND THE PROGRAM TELLS YOU — Since 1 April 2025 the classification has changed: the condominium administrator was 68.32.00, today it is 68.32.01 «Gestione di beni immobili per conto terzi»; the building was 97.00.02 and is now 97.00.10. Searching with the old words finds nothing, because the official titles no longer contain them: when the search finds nothing, the program tells you which two codes are the ones most needed.

THE LIST TRAVELS WITH THE PROGRAM — No installation needs the internet to have the codes: they arrive with the update, as already happens for the list of municipalities. Anyone can reload them by hand with «php artisan kondomanager:aggiorna-ateco».

AND YOU ALWAYS KNOW WHICH CLASSIFICATION THEY COME FROM — At the bottom of the search it says «Classificazione ATECO 2025, pubblicata da ISTAT». It is not an ornament: a list that does not say where it comes from ages silently, and a withdrawn code suggested by the program is wrong data. There is also a command that asks ISTAT whether a more recent revision has been published.

DETAILS — The search finds a code even written without the dots («432201»), and looks for the words separately, so «installazione ascensori» finds «Installazione di ascensori e scale mobili». Duplicates are gone: where a category and a subcategory carry the exact same title — 725 cases out of 920 — only the six-digit one is offered.
